Class GlyphLayout

java.lang.Object
org.adsl.client.view.gui.GlyphLayout
public final class GlyphLayout extends Object
Pure (no-JavaFX) layout maths for the ChristmasChalk PNG bitmap font.

Numbers are composed at runtime from single-glyph PNGs (0–9, x, minus) instead of one pre-baked PNG per value. This class owns the two pieces that can be reasoned about without a scene graph: tokenising a string into glyph asset names, and computing each glyph's top-left position from the font metrics emitted by tools/GlyphAtlasGenerator.

All stored metrics are in oversampled (2×) pixels; place(String, GlyphLayout.Metrics) divides by scale so the returned placements are already in display space. Bearings are baked by the generator to point straight at the glyph image's top-left, so the layout here is a plain pen walk with no padding term.

    • tokens

      public static List<String> tokens(String text)
      Maps a string to glyph asset names: digits map to themselves, 'x' to "x", '-' to "minus". Returns null if any character has no glyph (caller should fall back to a live snapshot).

    • parse

      public static GlyphLayout.Metrics parse(String body)

    • place

      public static List<GlyphLayout.Placement> place(String text, GlyphLayout.Metrics m)
      Computes the display-space top-left of each glyph image for text. Returns an empty list when the string is unmappable or any glyph is absent from m (caller falls back).
